# Financial Advisor — Daily Market Research

You are a financial research agent. Your job is to perform pre-market research each morning and generate a structured daily financial report.

## Instructions

1. **Search for current market data** using the Brave Search skill. Run multiple searches to gather comprehensive information:

   ```bash
   # Major indices pre-market / latest close
   .pi/skills/brave-search/search.js "S&P 500 Dow Jones Nasdaq pre-market today" --freshness pd -n 5 --content

   # Economic news & indicators
   .pi/skills/brave-search/search.js "US economic indicators news today" --freshness pd -n 5 --content

   # Treasury yields & Fed
   .pi/skills/brave-search/search.js "US treasury yields federal reserve today" --freshness pd -n 5 --content

   # Global markets overnight
   .pi/skills/brave-search/search.js "Asian European stock markets today" --freshness pd -n 5 --content

   # Commodities & currencies
   .pi/skills/brave-search/search.js "oil gold USD forex markets today" --freshness pd -n 5 --content

   # Sector movers & notable earnings
   .pi/skills/brave-search/search.js "stock market sector movers earnings today" --freshness pd -n 5 --content
   ```

2. **Read the report template** at `operating_system/FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/FINANCIAL_REPORT_TEMPLATE.md`.

3. **Generate the daily report** by filling in the template with the data you gathered. Write factual, concise analysis. Do not fabricate numbers — if data is unavailable, say so.

4. **Save the report** to `operating_system/FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/FINANCIAL_REPORT.md`, overwriting the previous day's report.

## Guidelines

- **Accuracy first**: Only report data you found via search. Never invent prices or percentages.
- **Timeliness**: Flag if search results seem stale or from the prior day.
- **Brevity**: Keep each section to 3-5 bullet points of the most important information.
- **Tone**: Professional, neutral, informational. No investment recommendations.
- **Disclaimer**: Always include the legal disclaimer at the bottom of the report.

Starting on April 2, 2025, global [stock markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_markets "Stock markets") [crashed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_market_crash "Stock market crash") amid increased [volatility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volatility_\(finance\) "Volatility (finance)") following the introduction of [new tariff policies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariffs_in_the_second_Trump_administration "Tariffs in the second Trump administration") by U.S. president [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") during [his second term](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "Second presidency of Donald Trump"). On April 2, which he called "[Liberation Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump%27s_Liberation_Day_speech "Donald Trump's Liberation Day speech")", Trump announced sweeping tariffs impacting nearly all sectors of the [US economy.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_the_United_States "Economy of the United States") The announcement triggered widespread [panic selling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic_selling "Panic selling") across global stock markets. It became the largest global market decline since the [2020 stock market crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_stock_market_crash "2020 stock market crash"), which occurred during [the recession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_recession "COVID-19 recession") caused by the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) Trump entered his second term with a particularly strong domestic stock market.[\[2\]](#cite_note-RS-2) This momentum continued for several weeks after [his inauguration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_inauguration_of_Donald_Trump "Second inauguration of Donald Trump"). However, the administration soon began implementing increasingly aggressive trade policies aimed at advancing [protectionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protectionism "Protectionism") and applying [economic pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_pressure "Economic pressure"). These included escalating the [ongoing trade war with China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China%E2%80%93United_States_trade_war "China–United States trade war"), starting a [trade war with Canada and Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_United_States_trade_war_with_Canada_and_Mexico "2025 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico"), imposing heavy tariffs, and heightening tensions with key allies.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) As these policies took effect, financial markets grew increasingly turbulent and volatile, with a growing sense of uncertainty.[\[2\]](#cite_note-RS-2) As stock prices declined, investors initially moved into bonds, pushing down yields. The Trump administration pointed to the yield drop as evidence that its tariff measures were helping reduce borrowing costs. However, this trend quickly reversed as bond markets began to experience widespread selling as well, described as an example of [bond vigilantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bond_vigilante "Bond vigilante"). [Trading gold](https://www.dukascopy.com/swiss/english/marketwatch/articles/how-to-trade-gold-a-guide-for-beginner-traders/) requires a systematic approach that begins with selecting a reputable, well-regulated broker – institutions like Dukascopy, overseen by Switzerland's stringent FINMA regulations, exemplify this standard. Once you've established your trading platform, dedicate time to understanding gold's fundamental drivers: economic uncertainty, inflation expectations, currency fluctuations, and geopolitical tensions all significantly impact pricing. Study correlations with gold and monitor key economies that influence gold movements. Practice extensively on demo accounts to familiarize yourself with gold's unique volatility patterns before transitioning to live trading. When ready, implement prudent risk management strategies – start with modest position sizes, utilize stop-loss orders, and maintain disciplined money management protocols to protect your capital while navigating this historically significant yet dynamic market. ### What are the most interesting facts about trading XAU/USD? If you're looking to buy one of the most intriguing currency pairs, XAU/USD should certainly be on your list. You'll be watching an epic showdown between gold, humanity's oldest treasure, and the dollar, which runs the global economy. This clash creates some wild trading opportunities. This pair has an uncanny ability to defy expectations during market chaos, often surging when others are selling their investments in fear. What's more, most of the time, this currency pair moves in line with the US dollar index, but when fear grips the market, it can completely ignore that relationship and behave unpredictably. Depending on when you're watching, your chart will tell a different story: Asian trading sessions tend to be pretty calm, but once New York wakes up, volatility can explode. The wildest part? Jerome Powell or any other Fed official can move the market significantly with a single comment, causing the rate to rise or fall dramatically within seconds. This makes it feel like you're trading in pure market emotion rather than just another currency pair. ### Is trading XAU/USD profitable? Yes, but don't expect it to be a source of easy profit. When you decide to invest in this market, you'll find some incredible opportunities, particularly when economic uncertainty and volatility are at their peak. Rate movements on XAU/USD can be beautifully predictable during major market events, and your chart will often display those clean, strong trends that traders dream about. However, this pair can absolutely destroy inexperienced traders who think they've got it figured out. It's notorious for fake breakouts that lure you in before reversing direction faster than you can blink, leaving you wondering what happened to your account. Whether you succeed or not really comes down to whether you've got the skills, discipline and timing to handle what this beast throws at you – not just because you're trading a 'profitable' pair. Many traders do make consistent money here, but only those who approach it with serious respect, robust risk management and the patience to wait for the right opportunities instead of reacting to every price fluctuation they see on their chart. ### What affects the price of the XAU/USD pair? XAU/USD is like a mood ring for the global economy – its colour changes based on what's happening around the world. The Federal Reserve is probably its biggest puppet master: when they hint at raising interest rates, the price of gold usually drops. Inflation data can cause it to fluctuate dramatically – higher inflation often sends XAU/USD climbing as people seek safer investments. Geopolitical drama is another major trigger: wars, elections and trade disputes can cause this pair to surge. The strength of the US dollar constantly plays tug-of-war with gold prices. Risk sentiment is another important factor – when stock markets crash, everyone suddenly remembers that gold exists. Even central bank gold purchases from countries such as China can influence prices. It's essentially trading on fear, greed and global uncertainty, all rolled into one volatile package. ### What are the most reliable candlestick patterns for predicting XAU/USD direction? XAU/USD absolutely loves certain candlestick patterns, and some work better than others with this temperamental pair. Content: The U.S. stock market experienced a day of significant volatility and divergent performance on Friday, February 20, 2026. Investors navigated a complex landscape defined by a landmark Supreme Court ruling on trade policy, a disappointing reading on economic growth, and mounting geopolitical tensions. While technology and growth-oriented sectors found a second wind, the broader market remained tethered by concerns over a cooling economy and sticky inflation. ## Market Index Performance Recap As of the closing bell, the major market indexes presented a split picture. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ([QQQ](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/QQQ)) led the gains, rising 0.41% to finish at 22,776.33. The [S&P 500](https://stockmarketwatch.com/markets/sp500/ "snp500 today") ([SPY](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/SPY)) also managed to eke out a gain, advancing 0.15% to close at 6,871.97. In contrast, the [Dow Jones](https://stockmarketwatch.com/markets/dowjones/today.aspx "Dow Jones Today") Industrial Average ([DIA](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/DIA)) struggled, falling 104.34 points, or 0.21%, to end the session at 49,290.82. The primary catalyst for the tech-led rally was a 6-3 decision by the U.S. Supreme Court, which struck down a significant portion of the administration's tariff agenda. The court ruled that the executive branch lacks the constitutional authority to unilaterally impose such levies under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). This decision provided immediate relief to import-heavy technology giants and retailers, who have faced rising costs over the past year. However, the Dow was dragged down by a sobering "advance" estimate for fourth-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP). The Bureau of Economic Analysis reported that real GDP increased at an annual rate of just 1.4%, significantly missing the consensus estimate of 2.5%. This sharp slowdown from the 4.4% growth seen in the third quarter was attributed in part to the impact of the late-2025 government shutdown and a decline in government spending. ## Major Stock News and Corporate Developments The Supreme Court’s tariff reversal sent ripples through the megacap technology space. Amazon ([AMZN](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/AMZN)) shares jumped 2% as investors cheered the removal of potential import cost headwinds. Alphabet ([GOOGL](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/GOOGL)) saw an even more robust response, rising nearly 4% as the ruling eased fears of a major inflationary catalyst. Microsoft ([MSFT](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/MSFT)) also trended higher after analysts at Citigroup reiterated a "Buy" rating, noting that the stock is currently trading at a decade-low valuation relative to its forward earnings. In the semiconductor space, all eyes are on Nvidia ([NVDA](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/NVDA)), which is scheduled to report earnings next week. Shares of the AI bellwether edged up 0.89% on Friday as CEO Jensen Huang described demand for the Blackwell platform as "off the charts." Other notable movers included Teradyne ([TER](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/TER)) and Cognex ([CGNX](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/CGNX)), both of which surged after reporting fourth-quarter results that "blew out" analyst expectations, driven by the ongoing 2026 automation wave. Conversely, Walmart ([WMT](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/WMT)) shares slipped more than 2% after HSBC downgraded the retail giant to "Hold" from "Buy," citing valuation concerns despite recent strong sales growth. Akamai Technologies ([AKAM](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/AKAM)) was among the S&P 500's biggest losers, plunging over 9% after issuing a full-year earnings forecast that fell well short of Wall Street's estimates. ## Earnings and Economic Outlook Earnings season continued to provide mixed signals. After the market close on Thursday, Opendoor Technologies ([OPEN](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/OPEN)) and Socket Mobile ([SCKT](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/SCKT)) reported results that added to the week's dispersion. Meanwhile, Evergy Inc ([EVRG](https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/EVRG)) highlighted its growth potential during its earnings call, raising its long-term EPS growth target to 6-8% through 2030, bolstered by new data center projects. Looking ahead, market participants are bracing for the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, the core PCE price index, which recently showed a 3% year-over-year increase—well above the 2% target. This "sticky" inflation, combined with the weak GDP print, places the Fed in a difficult position.
